svg.text: The agentic platform in one picture
One front door, one identity per agent, one gateway out, one register: how agents are admitted, contained and watched.
A tier opens only once the roles it needs are staffed. Humans raise an
agent's autonomy; machines can only lower it.
Tiers: C no-code, read-only · R read tools · W writes · P privileged (the
Workspace super-admin agent, Wall-E) · X general capability, not opened

Audit logs and telemetry: every action, model call and admin change, stored immutably in the EU (400 days to 10 years by data class); sensitive-data scanning on the
Detections: Google's detections (Security Command Center) for every tier, paging the platform owner; the privileged tier adds an outsourced monitoring desk (people on
call, using a SIEM, a security monitoring tool); every finding names an owner and a deadline
The independent controller (Eve, no model in its approve or halt path): watches the agents and the human administrators, reports to a person independent of the agent's
owner, can halt an agent's actions; its evidence is copied daily to a witness outside the tenant
Evaluation: a blind human grader scores a sample of every writing agent's work (tier W and above) after admission; seeded faults run before admission and monthly; a
A hundredth read-only agent costs a register row, a factory run and a budget line; every writing agent also needs a named blind grader, and grading capacity is what limits the count (P25).
Two grades of control, tagged on every box: what Google or code refuses, and what is only detected. A content screen is detection, even when set to block.
A privileged agent costs more than a read-only one: a second person, an outsourced monitoring desk, a witness outside the tenant and a signed deviation.

Status on 2026-10-01: designed, not built. Agent Gateway, Agent Registry and Agent Identity on Agent Runtime are GA; Agent Identity on Cloud Run is Preview (P5). Full design: the agentic-platform wiki, 01-hld.md.
